chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The people crowded together on Friday during the rule of ʿAlī عليه السلام in Kūfah, and they killed a man; so he paid his blood-money to his family from the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.إِمْرَةِ عَلِيٍّ: the rule or governance of ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.فَوَدَى: so he compensated or paid ransom/blood-money

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah when a person is killed in a crowd and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that when a man was killed in a crowd on Friday during the rule of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in Kūfah, his diyah was paid to his family from the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims. It indicates a legal principle concerning cases where death occurs in a public crush and no specific killer is identified, placing financial responsibility on the public treasury.
